paid-speaking.route: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program (honorarium rules)

remote-work.detail: Visitors (ESTA or B visa) may not take employment; the State Department pages list meetings, conferences and negotiations but do not address remote work for a foreign employer either way.

laws.rule: Puerto Rico allows cannabis only for authorised medical use under Law 42-2017 (Ley MEDICINAL), with a physician's recommendation and the required ID; recreational use is not permitted. US federal law also applies.

In Culebra National Wildlife Refuge (Culebra and nearby cays, run by the US Fish and Wildlife Service) it is prohibited to harass, hunt or possess birds, lizards, snakes, turtles, crabs or any other species; to collect or possess live or dead coral; to collect live or dead plants; or to bring in or release domestic or wild animals. Fishing is governed by the Puerto Rico Department of Natural and Environmental Resources.

Cayo Luis Peña and Culebrita in Culebra National Wildlife Refuge are reached by boat only, and visitors arrange their own transport. Other refuge areas need authorisation because of ecological sensitivity and unexploded military ordnance; the Flamenco Peninsula and surrounding cays and reefs are closed to the public. If you see a suspect object: recognise, retreat, report. The Culebrita lighthouse (Municipality of Culebra) is closed.

items.text: Law 42-2017 (Puerto Rico Medical Cannabis Law) allows only medicinal and scientific use. Use needs a recommendation from an authorised physician and an ID issued by the Medical Cannabis Regulatory Board (Junta Reglamentadora del Cannabis Medicinal) of the Department of Health, and is limited to homes and private places.

The law reaffirms the ban on recreational cannabis, including smoking it; recreational use is dealt with under Law 4, the Controlled Substances Act. Regulation 9038 also prohibits possessing, cultivating, transporting, donating or selling cannabis for recreational purposes.
A Department of Health release dated 23 April 2026 says the Board will keep applying Law 42-2017 and Regulation 9038 and will review changes step by step with federal agencies.

The order also declares Friday 27 November 2026 and the time from noon on Thursday 31 December 2026 as holidays for executive-branch public servants, and allows days off (charged to leave) on 20 and 25 November and 24 December 2026. The Governor sets the full 2027 list by proclamation; its text was not read.
